notes.20: Candidates write a paragraph-length summary of no more than 100 words about an aspect of the text in Exercise 3 . Exercise 4, 5 and 6 assess their reading and writing abilities, so Language marks are awarded separately from the content marks. Most candidates managed to adhere to the prescribed word limit while summarising the main points from the text. The weaker candidates tended to lift big chunks of the text which did not show their own writing skills or ability to identify the main points of a text. Exercise 5
notes.21: Candidates write a short functional prose of approximately 120 words as an e-mail in response to a series of 3 prompts. Candidates mostly performed well on this task; however, their written work has errors in spelling of everyday vocabulary and grammatical structures. It is also important to stick to the word limit of the task. Exercise 6
notes.22: Candidates write a longer piece of continuous prose of approximately 200 words. The topic was found to be engaging for almost all the candidates. Most candidates discussed both sides of the given statement and provided a logical conclusion. The quality of written work is variable. More attention to spelling and a range of correct grammatical structures will further raise the standards of IGCSE Hindi as a Second Language. HINDI AS A SECOND LANGUAGE
notes.key_messages: In order to raise the standards, candidates need to ensure to: • Pay more attention to spellings, vocabulary and grammatical structures. • Follow the word limit prescribed for each question. • Read the question carefully before answering it.
notes.general_comments: The performance of candidates varied from very good to average and a few below average. Some more able candidates seem well prepared to attempt all the questions. Some weaker candidates could identify and select relevant information from the text, but had difficulty in understanding the connection between ideas, opinions and writer’s intention. Spelling and Grammatical errors were widespread.
